newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian newcomers offer Internet quotes, news. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Belgian newcomers offer Internet quotes, news. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: A Belgian start-up firm plans to sell real-time stock prices and financial news on an Internet web site, and says it will give retail investors access to information previously enjoyed only by professional traders.

Without backing from traditional market players, two young Belgians in their twenties have signed contracts with several stock exchanges, British money and securities broker Harlow Butler and news agency AFX to resell quotes and news.
World Online Quote And Trading System (WOQATS), founded last year, will launch commercialy on May 21.
"WOQATS will turn an ordinary PC into a true trading room terminal," founder Dimitri Verboomen, 27, told Reuters on Friday.
Net surfers who access the www.woqats.com (corrects from www.tradinghouse.com) site can sign up as customers. Payments can be made by credit card or invoice.
For about $300 (10,500 Belgian francs) a month, clients will get real-time stock prices from nine markets, cross rates for 20 currencies and financial news.
Verboomen said the service would be a tenth of the price of that from traditional vendors to investment professionals, "and it works anywhere in the world".

The market for trading room price and news distribution has long been dominated by a few large players, such as Reuters Holdings Plc, Bloomberg LP and Dow Jones Markets (formerly Telerate), who all have proprietary world-wide distribution systems for electronic information.

The information revolution means market majors face local competition, as national vendors sell news and prices on videotext, cable television and other networks. The Internet gives a global reach to upstarts like WOQATS.
WOQATS says it has contracts with NASDAQ, the London, Paris, Swiss and German stock exchanges. It says it is talking with the New York stock exchange, AMEX, the Brussels bourse and others.
The company plans to add bond and money market yields and options prices later this year and expects to add trading facilities to its network.
WOQATS director Raphael Fuchs, 25, said its technology automatically refreshes the price data using an application in the JAVA 1.1 language.
WOQATS aimed to give customers information on European stocks American competitors did not yet offer and fresher updates on stocks than offered by Internet vendors in Europe.
"Our strategy is one-stop shopping -- all the markets, news and soon trading facilities," Fuchs said.
